text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Socialist caucus leader Imre Szekeres delivered the opening remarks at Parliament's first session of 1997, in the absence of the prime minister. Opposition MPs rejected the government's view that Hungary has moved beyond crisis and is positioned to join the EU and NATO as over-optimistic and launched an extended attack on the government's repurchase of Polgari Bank.

- Ivan Peto could be challenged as Free Democrat parliamentary caucus chief when the group holds its annual conference on Sunday, as several party MPs are unhappy with his handling of the Tocsik scandal.
- The board of directors of Raiffeisen Unicbank Rt. will propose an equity increase of between HUF 500 million and HUF 1 billion at the March AGM.
- The National Sugar Beet Producers Association has called on members to suspend sugar beet sales to sugar factories, said association head Geza Szoke.

- A Molotov cocktail was tossed into a Greek restaurant in Budapest's Andrassy ut on Monday and burned down the roof structure, causing several millions of forints in damages but no personal injuries.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- NATO Secretary General Javier Solana flatly denied on Monday that any countries admitted to the alliance will become 'second class' members, regardless of whether the issue is examined in terms of NATO-Russian ties, or security guarantees.
- Slovak armed forces chief of staff Jozef Tuchyna arrived to Budapest Monday for a three-day visit.

- Speculation about the recent Hungarian-Slovak consultations on the Gabcikovo hydropower project could adversely affect Hungary's case against the project, the lawyer representing Hungary warned yesterday.

- In a report on the privatisation of the Hungarian Electricity Works and the domestic energy sector, the State Audit Office warns that the continuity and safety of the energy supply is not assured, since the financing of investments between 1997 and 2000 has not been established.

- The Stock Exchange Council yesterday approved the sale of Vektor Broker's membership on the exchange to financial services company Moresbi Penzugyi Szolgaltato Kft, while the State Money and Capital Market Supervision again prolonged its ban on securities trading by Vektor Broker until March 31.
- Ronald Reising will become deputy managing director for finances at Matav from February 24.
- An off-duty plainclothes police sergeant caught one of two men attempting to steal HUF 6.5 million from two couriers near the Astoria hotel in downtown Budapest yesterday.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The truck manufacturer Raba Rt. published tender details today for three of its subsidiaries.

- A total of 2.3 million cars used M1 toll highway between Gyor and Hegyeshalom last year, 80 percent of the travellers on M1 were foreigners, according to figures from the First Hungarian Concession Highway Rt.
NEPSZABADSAG
- A border guards logistics officer in Budapest was detained at the weekend on suspicion of stealing firearms and ammunition.
